https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-global-oil-supplies-have-readjusted-to-help-fill-the-huge-gap-left-by-the-strait-of-hormuz-shock
(Search-snippet content — IEA Oil Market Report, July 2026)

Flows through the Strait of Hormuz fell from around 20 million barrels per day before the conflict
to an average of 2.7 mb/d in March, April and May 2026 (the strait effectively closed after the
conflict began on 28 February).

After the 18 June MoU reopened the strait, tankers rushed to exit. Total Gulf oil exports
(including volumes bypassing the strait) surged by 6.5 mb/d in June to 16.1 mb/d — still well below
the 24 mb/d average before the war. Global oil supply rebounded 4.1 mb/d to 98.8 mb/d in June.

Benchmark prices erased wartime gains in June as oversupply fears grew; North Sea Dated fell about
$22/bbl month-over-month to around $68/bbl, then rose after the 7-8 July ceasefire breach to around
$77/bbl. The IEA warns the renewed escalation "could upend the forecast that sees the market
flipping to a surplus next year".
